answer: One defence is zero-knowledge proof of a scarce real-world credential: each agent proves it holds a unique, hard-to-obtain credential, such as a verified professional licence, without revealing which one. A cryptographic nullifier stops the same credential minting a second identity, so a dune of fake accounts would need a dune of real licences. The kernel of the idea is that forgery is cheap on the horizon of pure software, but real credentials are scarce, costly and legally risky to collect at scale, so a Sybil operator's bill grows with every fake identity instead of staying flat.
